newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: TAG Heuer cuts costs, aims upmarket.
newsitem.headline: TAG Heuer cuts costs, aims upmarket.

text.p: Swiss watchmaker TAG Heuer, which went public in September, says it is cutting costs while sticking with a strategy of going upmarket for better returns.

Christian Viros, TAG Heuer's chief executive, speaking to journalists at a presentation of 1996 annual results, said the company is targeting revenue growth of "10 percent plus" in 1997, and was also seeking to return more to shareholders.
Its 1996 sales rose two percent to 717,000 units from 703,000 in 1995. In value terms, sales rose 10.6 percent to 419.7 million francs ($290.5 million), up from 379.6 million.

The company's stock was floated in an initial public offering in Switzerland and New York in September 1996. It was quoted at 195.25 Swiss francs on Wednesday, above the year's low of 186.00 of April 1 but below its IPO price of 245 francs.
The IPO brought the company additional proceeds of 301 million francs, which was used in part to reduce debt.
The company reported a total shareholders' (equity) deficit of 29.7 million francs in 1996, based on liabilities totalling 293.6 million francs against assets of 263.9 million.
This compared with 514.2 million in liabilities in 1995 and assets of 243.5 milllion, which produced an equity deficit of 270.7 million in 1995.
Viros said the company, which paid no dividend for 1996, would seek to return more to shareholders in the future.
"Our mandate is to optimise shareholder value," Viros said.
"The fundamentals have not changed since we did the road show" (for the IPO), he added.

With respect to the IPO, Viros said the sharp share price drop may have been due partly to a misallocation. "You have to ask if those willing to buy (the shares) were willing to buy and sell (them) the same day," Viros said.
Viros said current strategy included reviewing costs. The company, Switzerland's fifth-largest watchmaker in terms of revenue, will dispose of its corporate jet, for example.
At the same time changes are expected in management.
"We are working on restructuring the board," he said, saying in that area, too, TAG Heuer "should make some announcements very shortly."

It also plans to introduce a new line of watches which will conform to its strategy of increasing its per-unit price, in line with its top objective of achieving "institutional status for TAG Heuer as a prestigious brand." It is also planning to introduce a line of ladies' watches.
Estimated retail price per unit has risen to 1,500 Swiss francs in 1996 from 950 francs five years ago. About 40 percent of its products are sold above the average price.

Asian and Australian sales were disappointing, showing only a 3.1 percent increase, partly a result of the weak yen. At the same time, the company said it had distribution problems in Japan resulting from inadequacy of stocks, and was taking steps to address the problems.
"Japan sells through wholesalers. We want to get closer to the market," Viros said.
Sales in the Americas rose 17.9 percent and they also rose 15.5 percent in Europe in 1996, he said.
-- Zurich Editorial, +41 1 631 7340 ($ = 1.444 Swiss Francs)
